topicName: Cloud Data Fusion: Data Integration ETL
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Cloud Data Fusion: Data Integration ETL on Google Cloud (GCP)"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Cloud Data Fusion is a fully managed, cloud-native data integration service that helps you build and manage data pipelines. It provides a graphical interface to develop ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) pipelines without coding, making data integration accessible to a wider range of users. This tutorial will guide you through the basics of using Cloud Data Fusion for data integration on Google Cloud Platform (GCP)."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A Google Cloud Platform (GCP) account with billing enabled."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Basic understanding of ETL concepts."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Familiarity with Google Cloud Console."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Enable the Cloud Data Fusion API"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before you can use Cloud Data Fusion, you need to enable the API in your GCP project. Follow these steps:"},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Go to the Google Cloud Console (console.cloud.google.com)."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Select your project."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"In the search bar, type 'Cloud Data Fusion' and select it."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Click 'Enable'."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Create a Cloud Data Fusion Instance"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Now, create a Cloud Data Fusion instance. This instance will host your data pipelines."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"In the Cloud Data Fusion page, click 'Create instance'."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Provide a name for your instance (e.g., 'my-data-fusion-instance')."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Choose a region and zone where you want to deploy the instance."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Select the edition (Basic, Enterprise, or Developer). For this tutorial, the 'Basic' edition is sufficient."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Configure the instance size based on your needs. The default settings are usually adequate for small to medium-sized projects."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Click 'Create'. The instance creation process may take some time."},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Access the Cloud Data Fusion Web UI"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once the instance is created, you can access the Cloud Data Fusion web UI."},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"In the Cloud Data Fusion page, click on the instance name you created."},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Click 'View Instance' to open the Cloud Data Fusion web UI in a new tab."},{"order":25,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 4: Build a Simple ETL Pipeline"},{"order":26,"type":"paragraph","text":"Let's create a simple ETL pipeline that reads data from a Cloud Storage bucket, transforms it, and writes it to another Cloud Storage bucket."},{"order":27,"type":"bullet_point","text":"In the Cloud Data Fusion web UI, click on 'Studio'."},{"order":28,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Drag and drop a 'GCS Bucket' source plugin onto the canvas."},{"order":29,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Configure the 'GCS Bucket' source plugin by providing the bucket name, path, and file format (e.g., CSV). You'll need a Cloud Storage bucket with some sample data. Ensure the service account used by Cloud Data Fusion has read access to the bucket."},{"order":30,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Drag and drop a 'Transform' plugin (e.g., 'Expression') onto the canvas."},{"order":31,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Connect the 'GCS Bucket' source to the 'Expression' transform plugin by dragging a connector from the source to the transform."},{"order":32,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Configure the 'Expression' transform plugin to perform a simple transformation, such as concatenating two fields or converting a field to uppercase. For example, you can use the expression 'upper(column1)' to convert the 'column1' field to uppercase."},{"order":33,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Drag and drop a 'GCS Bucket' sink plugin onto the canvas."},{"order":34,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Connect the 'Expression' transform to the 'GCS Bucket' sink plugin."},{"order":35,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Configure the 'GCS Bucket' sink plugin by providing the destination bucket name, path, and file format. Ensure the service account used by Cloud Data Fusion has write access to the destination bucket."},{"order":36,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 5: Run the Pipeline"},{"order":37,"type":"paragraph","text":"Now that you've built the pipeline, you can run it."},{"order":38,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Click 'Save' to save the pipeline."},{"order":39,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Click 'Deploy' to deploy the pipeline."},{"order":40,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Click 'Run' to start the pipeline execution."},{"order":41,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can monitor the pipeline execution in the 'Runs' tab. Once the pipeline completes successfully, you should see the transformed data in the destination Cloud Storage bucket."},{"order":42,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 6: Clean Up"},{"order":43,"type":"paragraph","text":"To avoid incurring unnecessary charges, remember to clean up the resources you created."},{"order":44,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Delete the Cloud Data Fusion instance."},{"order":45,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Delete the Cloud Storage buckets you created for the source and destination data (if you created them specifically for this tutorial)."},{"order":46,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":47,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial provided a basic introduction to using Cloud Data Fusion for data integration ETL on Google Cloud Platform. Cloud Data Fusion offers a wide range of plugins and features to build complex data pipelines for various use cases. Explore the documentation and experiment with different plugins to learn more about its capabilities."}]
